GOD GROUNDS MORALITY AND HIGHER PURPOSE · SJ THOMASON
"we're all put here for a reason"

Thomason grants that atheists can construct satisfying everyday purposes, then states her stronger view that individual gifts belong within an assigned higher calling.

"

MORAL FACTS AND MEANINGFUL LIVES DO NOT REQUIRE GOD · SCOTT CLIFTON
"I think ultimately morality reduces to well-being"

Clifton distinguishes objective facts about conscious experience from intrinsic value and categorical obligation while explaining the positive basis of his secular moral account.

tags.text:
Equivocation
LOGICAL FALLACY
Shifting the meaning of a key word or phrase during the argument, making the reasoning seem stronger than it is.
After granting atheists everyday purposes, Thomason treats cosmic accident and eventual forgetting as showing that atheist life has no meaning.
OPEN THE REFERENCE PAGE FOR MORE.

Red herring
LOGICAL FALLACY
Diverting attention from the issue under dispute to a related but less relevant point, leaving the original challenge insufficiently answered.
Asked why uncreated God is not purposeless, Thomason turns from God’s purpose to human belief and external accountability.
OPEN THE REFERENCE PAGE FOR MORE.

Begging the question
LOGICAL FALLACY
Assuming, directly or indirectly, the very point that needs to be established, so the conclusion is smuggled into the premises.
Thomason presents Jesus taking human punishment as already reconciling God’s perfect mercy with perfect justice.
